title: Python: LRU cache
prompt: Implement an LRU cache class in Python with O(1) get and put, using a dict and a doubly linked list. Include type hints and a short usage example.

title: Math: word problem
prompt: A train leaves city A at 9:00 traveling at 80 km/h. Another train leaves city B, 360 km away, at 10:00 traveling toward A at 100 km/h. At what time do they meet, and how far from city A? Solve step by step.

title: Explain: speculative decoding
prompt: Explain how speculative decoding speeds up large language model inference. Cover the draft model, the verification step, and why the output distribution is unchanged.

title: Writing: email
prompt: Write a polite email to a colleague asking them to review a pull request that refactors the authentication module before Friday.

title: Translation
prompt: Translate the following paragraph into Chinese: Large language models generate text one token at a time, which makes decoding memory-bound. Speculative decoding drafts several tokens cheaply and verifies them in parallel with the target model.

title: SQL
prompt: Given tables orders(id, customer_id, amount, created_at) and customers(id, name, country), write a SQL query that returns the top 5 countries by total order amount in 2024, with the number of distinct customers per country.

title: Summarize
prompt: Summarize the main ideas of the transformer architecture in 6 bullet points for a software engineer who is new to deep learning.

title: Long: LLM inference tutorial
prompt: Write a comprehensive tutorial on large language model inference. Cover, in order and in full detail: model loading and quantization, the KV cache, batching strategies, memory and bandwidth limits, speculative decoding, and serving frameworks. Use concrete numbers and small code examples. Do not skip any section and keep writing until everything above is explained at length.

title: Long: history of computing
prompt: Write a long-form essay (3,000+ words) on the history of computing, from mechanical calculators to modern AI. Discuss at least ten major milestones, the people behind them, why each one changed the world, and how they built on each other. Write continuous prose, one well-developed paragraph after another, and do not stop until the full story is told.

title: Long: ML systems syllabus
prompt: Design a complete 15-week graduate course syllabus for "Machine Learning Systems". For each week provide: the topic, 3-5 learning objectives, required readings, one hands-on assignment with a detailed description, and one exam question with a model answer. Be thorough; this syllabus will be used directly in class.

title: Long: first-contact novel
prompt: Write the first three chapters of a science-fiction novel, about 3,000 words, about humanity's first contact with an alien species that communicates through music. Establish the setting, introduce the two main characters in rich detail, and dramatize the first meeting. Show, don't tell; include dialogue and sensory detail.

title: Long: train an LLM pipeline
prompt: Describe, step by step, the entire pipeline for training a 7B-parameter language model from scratch: data collection and cleaning, tokenizer training, pretraining objectives, distributed training setup, and evaluation. For each step, explain the decisions, the trade-offs, and the failure modes. Be exhaustive; a reader should be able to reproduce the whole pipeline from your text.

title: Long: PyTorch vs JAX
prompt: Compare PyTorch and JAX across 15 different dimensions, such as programming model, autograd, compilation, ecosystem, debugging, production deployment, and research usability. For each dimension, write a full paragraph with a concrete example. End with a recommendation for five different project types.

title: Long: spec-decode lecture notes
prompt: You are teaching a graduate course on efficient inference. Write your complete lecture notes on speculative decoding, about 8,000 tokens: motivation, the draft-verify framework, acceptance-rate and speedup mathematics, tree-based variants, implementation inside a real serving engine, and open problems. Write the notes as continuous prose in numbered sections; a student reading only your notes should understand the topic fully.

title: Long: distributed systems handbook
prompt: Write a handbook chapter (2,500+ words) titled "Building Reliable Distributed Systems", covering failure modes, retries and backoff, idempotency, consensus, observability, and testing. Include real-world war stories and end each section with a practical checklist.

title: Long: AI researcher interview
prompt: Write a long-form interview with a fictional AI researcher who has just built a system that invents its own programming language. Write at least 30 back-and-forth questions and answers, each answer a full paragraph, covering the motivation, the technical challenges, the ethical implications, and what happens next.

title: Long: AGI debate essay
prompt: Write a balanced debate essay (3,000 words) on whether AGI will be achieved by 2050. Present the strongest 8 arguments on each side, each developed in a full paragraph with evidence and counterpoints, then give your own synthesis and prediction.
